full_text_screens.principal_locator: Limitations and future directions, printed pp139–142 (PDF pp149–152)
source_stated_research_directions: Simulate non-normal and non-continuous indicators and inspect orthogonal contrast accuracy.
Simulate missingness under unbalanced groups, including deletion and full-information maximum likelihood.
Vary factor variance, loadings, and residuals to study partial strong invariance with unequal groups.
Ask whether formative or cross-loaded measurement models, and time-varying group membership, change the unbalanced contrast results.
full_text_screens.suitability_result: The future-work passages are empirical simulation extensions. No author-stated mathematical conjecture is recorded. The orthogonality arithmetic for this contrast code is a project-derived statement, proved in this repository, and is not an inventory target.

project_derived_followups.task: Under a fixed factor model, define an item-subset size budget and quantify information or prediction loss for an unweighted short-form score.
project_derived_followups.gate: Specify loadings, factor/noise covariance, identifiability conventions and loss; distinguish new empirical item development from a mathematical statement.

project_derived_followups.source_locator: Table 2.2 and equations (3.3)–(3.5); Chapter V discussion of non-orthogonality under imbalance
project_derived_followups.task: For these four codes, determine which sample-size-weighted products vanish under equal sizes and under the pattern of two equal large groups and two equal small groups, and evaluate equations (3.3)–(3.5) on the printed means.
project_derived_followups.gate: The codes and the means are the printed ones. The result is an identity for this design, not a general theorem about every contrast set.
project_derived_followups.status: proved in formalization/latent-contrasts for the printed codes and means
